posts.name: Shatner
posts.cooked:
In conventional SotM, the H mechanic allows villains to scale to the number of heroes opposing them. Vengeance offers a cool new mode of play where the number of villains scale to the number of players instead of the potency of the villain cards. As such, all the Vengeance villain decks and character cards lack the H mechanic. Is there a good way to convert the Vengeance villains to adopt the H mechanic so you can play them like a conventional, stand-alone villain?
 
 
 
Example: at the end of his turn, the Fright Train character card says he does 3 damage to the hero with the highest hp. Converting that to H-1 seems like it'd do the trick, because the default H assumption is 4 (with a minimum of 2 and a maximum of 5). However, Proletariat (and his clones) does 2 damage, which would convert to H-2 which would be zero damage in a 2 player game. Clearly this isn't as simple as replacing all damage values with H + (OriginalValue - 4).
 
 
 
 
 
Failing that, is there a number of players the Vengeance villains would be effective against (e.g. you can play against Proletariat as is provided you play against him with no more than 2 heroes... any more than that and he becomes too easy)?

posts.name: broccoli
posts.cooked:
Well, seeing as the idea of Vengeance is that you play against H of them, this mean that H villain cards get played each turn.  Thus, while you would still need to do something to their hp (multiplying by H might be too much, but scale it some), you could fairly easily make them scaling by playing them like a full Vengeance team.  Just let the specific villain play a card between each hero's turn, and it would be similar to playing against the V5, but just with one.

 

Edit: To be clear, you don't need to adjust their damage to scale with H, as they'll be playing H cards each full turn.

posts.name: Shatner
posts.cooked:
Speaking as the OP, I'd like to say that the intent behind this thread is not to be critical of Vengeance, but to make it easier to play it even more. The expansion is a fine one and my gaming group has really enjoyed it. However, I know that folks are going to want to mix and match the formats if they can ("Let's play with Ambuscade in the V5. It'd be fun and he shows up on so many of new the cards" or "Proletariat is awesome. We need to find a way to fight him as a stand-alone villian some time"), so I came to ask the forum how best to do that. If doing so is an unofficial variant, so be it, but the request is by an avid fan seeking to find MORE ways to play a great game, and the request is being made to other avid fans (I also have a BGG thread asking about this), not the developers of the game.
 
The fact that others want the same thing as me is great; more interest to drive the discussion. The tone others use in conveying that, however, is their own business and separate from the matter at hand: enhancing Vengeance's replayability. So moving on, someone over on BGG pointed out that the V5 villains have 20 card decks instead of the standard 25. Using broccoli's suggestion does mean you'll see the same cards way more often than you would normally because 1) the villain deck is being played H-times per round and 2) the villain deck has fewer cards to go through before it shuffles. That's not inherently bad, but it is something to be aware of.
 
Does anyone have an idea on how much to scale the villain's health by? Maybe hp * (1 + (H - 1)/2)... so you increase it by 100% if up against 3 heroes, 150% against 4 heroes, and 200% if up against 5 heroes.

Its not about what I feel. its about how I say it. 

 

/Should/ implies you are better than them and you know better. there are terms for this. Armchair quarterback. Backseat driver. And others. 

 

You have every right to your opinion, but there is an amount of common politeness and manners fall upon one to use when dealing with peoples work that they poured blood, sweat, and tears into. Telling them they did a labor of love wrong is not only rude, but downright brutal.

 

I do not like the Prequals. I never have said that George Lucas /should/ have done it a certain way. I was not on set. I never have made a movie. I have never acted in a movie. I have never written one. I have never been to hollywood or dealt with the people that make movies. I have never been involved in movie making.  I can express an opinion of dislike all I want, but i have no right to tell him how he /should/ have done it.

 

 

Shater - I have no issue with people looking to make house rules or custom rules, or variants of any type. By all means - explore those, they will only bring more awesomeness to this game.

 

I do however have an issue with people who affect an air of arrogance that they know better than others simply because they 'are' without any sort of experience with the actual product or process. Envisioner was not involved in the development of this expansion, he is entitled to his opinion as to what he would have liked to have seen, but not to a position that anyone /should/ have done anything differently.
